gen-fs-pencerio-outfit: A calligraphic hand with tightly clenched word shapes gives Pencerio its formal grace, and it is comfortable in small doses. But Outfit counters with plain sans lines bent like cable, unvarying in thickness and finishing their curves before they close.
gen-fs-pilcrow-rounded-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified, with a tall middle band and soft shifts in stroke weight. Pilcrow Rounded sits above it in smooth, plain outlines, so the headings feel friendly while the text stays gently shaded.
gen-fs-pilcrow-rounded-fs-karma: Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters close, like poured lead type, with a constant pen-pressure look. Yet it earns its keep big and brief, while Karma, a text serif, thins its joins gently without turning spindly.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-archivo: Pramukh Rounded bunches its glyphs tight, with open bowls tipped toward you like a ladle. Archivo follows in a similar build, its curves opening outward, and the heading font earns its keep when big and short.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-familjen-grote: Tightly bunched glyphs give Pramukh Rounded its look. Familjen Grotesk, a plain sans with bowls left unfinished on one side, shares that friendly build and adds a livelier tall lowercase.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-hind: Hind keeps its lowercase close to the capitals' height. Its curves match the stems exactly, which sets off the tightly bunched, ladle-bowled Pramukh Rounded and makes the shared friendliness the strongest thing here.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-hoover: Pramukh Rounded packs its glyphs tight, with large lowercase forms crowding the ascenders. Yet Hoover, a text serif with a generous eye in the e and compressed ascenders, would carry a long passage with a sturdy, refined ease.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-graduate: Friendly and neutral up top, with glyphs bunched tight. Graduate, a serif with generous white between letters and no thin strokes vanishing in glare, makes the dignified, bookish contrast the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-public-sans-fs-erode: Public Sans brings broad terminal gaps and a high x-height. Erode, a text serif, adds a lightly swelling stroke in each rounded letter, so the headings feel modern while the body reads editorial.
gen-fs-quicksand-gf-graduate: Short capitals among tall small letters mark Quicksand, whose tube-like stroke keeps a bright opening at every curve. Graduate, a serif, handles the dignified, bookish work with generous spacing and no contrast between stems and joins.
